enonce_intro_markdown: **Section B: Vocabulary (10 marks)**, in two parts: A) fill in the blanks of a passage about scientific progress, using words from a box (5 marks); B) match words with their definitions (5 marks).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A- Complete the passage with some of the words from the box (*scientists, laboratories, mass production, microchip, experiments, invention, researches, labour-saving, automatic, factories, vending machines*). Use a word or group of words only once.

"Experts claim that progress is being made in all scientific fields, and in most cases they are right. In **1.** …………..…..….all round the world, **2.** ……..………..….carry out **3.** …………..…..….and do important **4.** …………..…..…. into ways of improving technology. Machinery has already replaced large numbers of workers in many **5.** …………..…..…. and prices of electrical goods have been reduced by **6.** …………..…..…. Many of us are now quite used to the convenience of getting tickets, snacks and soft drinks from **7.** …………..…..…. and we are able to use **8.** …………..…..…. domestic appliances to make housework easier. Perhaps the **9.** …………..…..…. which has made the most dramatic difference to life in developed countries is the **10.** …………..…..….in our computers."

rappels_de_methode.texte: Filling gaps in a passage requires reading the whole sentence (and often the surrounding sentences) to identify grammatical clues (singular/plural, verb agreement, preposition) and semantic clues (which word logically fits the meaning), rather than matching words in isolation.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Filling vocabulary gaps requires reading the full sentence for grammatical clues (number, verb agreement) and semantic clues (logical meaning in context), not matching words in isolation.

### Corrigé détaillé
**1. laboratories** — "In laboratories all round the world" (a plural place where scientific work happens, matching 'all round the world').

**2. scientists** — "scientists carry out" (plural subject needed for the verb 'carry', the people who work in laboratories).

**3. experiments** — "carry out experiments" (fixed collocation: 'carry out experiments').

**4. researches** — "do important researches into" (fixed collocation: 'do research(es) into').

**5. factories** — "replaced large numbers of workers in many factories" (place where machinery replaces workers).

**6. mass production** — "prices... have been reduced by mass production" (the industrial process that lowers prices).

**7. vending machines** — "getting tickets, snacks and soft drinks from vending machines" (machines that dispense such items).

**8. automatic** — "automatic domestic appliances" (adjective describing appliances that work without manual operation).

**9. invention** — "the invention which has made the most dramatic difference" (a single noteworthy creation, matching the singular verb 'has made').

**10. microchip** — "the microchip in our computers" (the specific component responsible for computing advances).

### Piège à éviter
Do not confuse 'researches' (used here as a plural countable noun, acceptable in this fixed context) with the more common uncountable use of 'research': context and collocation should guide the choice, not just general vocabulary knowledge.

questions.enonce_markdown:
B- Match each word in Column A with its definition in Column B. Do not use any item more than once.

Column A: 1. bungalow, 2. packaging, 3. factory, 4. recycling, 5. habitat, 6. experimenting, 7. verdict, 8. resort, 9. blackmail, 10. symptom.

Column B: a. trying something out; b. describing an illness you can easily catch; c. getting money from people by threats; d. a place where people go on holiday; e. a decision in court; f. a place where an animal lives; g. using again, perhaps in another form; h. a place where goods are produced; i. paper or plastic for wrapping; j. a one-storey house.

rappels_de_methode.texte: Matching vocabulary to definitions requires identifying the precise semantic core of each word (its essential defining feature) and eliminating already-matched options systematically, since exactly one definition corresponds to each word in a one-to-one matching exercise.

questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Matching vocabulary to definitions requires identifying the precise semantic core of each word and eliminating already-matched options systematically, since each word has exactly one corresponding definition.

### Corrigé détaillé
**1. bungalow → j** (a one-storey house)

**2. packaging → i** (paper or plastic for wrapping)

**3. factory → h** (a place where goods are produced)

**4. recycling → g** (using again, perhaps in another form)

**5. habitat → f** (a place where an animal lives)

**6. experimenting → a** (trying something out)

**7. verdict → e** (a decision in court)

**8. resort → d** (a place where people go on holiday)

**9. blackmail → c** (getting money from people by threats)

**10. symptom → b** (describing an illness you can easily catch — by elimination, the last remaining pair)

### Piège à éviter
Proceed by elimination: match the most unambiguous pairs first (bungalow/j, packaging/i, factory/h are very distinctive), then use process of elimination for the remaining, less obvious pairs to avoid errors caused by superficially similar definitions.
